topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and sets expectations for understanding cancer biology.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: They define cancer as a multistep disease driven by genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation, and consider the experimental models used to study these cellular properties.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and malignant progression
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the biological and histological characteristics distinguishing benign from invasive and metastatic tumours, including the stepwise progression to malignancy.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and classification
topics.groupedBecause: It outlines the standard naming conventions and clinical exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumours based on tissue origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the pathophysiological mechanisms through which primary and metastatic tumours cause disease, organ dysfunction, and death.

topics.label: Comparative tumor incidence across species
topics.groupedBecause: They survey the incidence and prevalence of benign and malignant tumours across human populations and diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Cancer presentation and screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the clinical rationale, histological basis, and diagnostic methods used to screen for and detect pre-malignant and malignant tumours.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture by revisiting the learning outcomes and providing reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
